note: The first attacker-controlled byte selects the target architecture/mode pair, steering execution into a specific decoder path.
All remaining attacker-controlled bytes are passed directly into Capstone's disassembler as instruction stream input.
For EVM-selected inputs, the first payload byte is interpreted as an opcode and validated against the opcode table.
When the opcode is PUSH1..PUSH32, the opcode value determines how many immediate bytes will be copied from attacker input.
The decoder copies the attacker-controlled immediate bytes into the instruction object; this is the memory-safety sink reached by the crafted input path.
